children: According to CNBC, Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison’s settlement with state attorneys general over antitrust concerns requires the combined company to release at least 30 films in theaters in 2027 and 2028 and at least 32 films in 2029, 2030 and 2031 as part of its planned acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The agreement also requires at least 20 wide releases in more than 2,000 theaters in each of the first two years after closing, rising to at least 21 in the following three years, and says at least 20% of annual releases must be tentpole films defined as having budgets of at least $50 million. If Paramount misses the annual quotas, it faces penalties of $30 million per film, with 90% of the money going to film workers and 10% to the National Association of Attorneys General.

title: Paramount Skydance Settlement Requires At Least 30 Films a Year After Warner Bros. Discovery Deal
